extraction.name: LongBench
extraction.description: LongBench is the first bilingual, multi-task benchmark for long context understanding, comprising 21 datasets across 6 task categories in both English and Chinese. It covers key long-text application areas including single-doc QA, multi-doc QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code completion, with an average length of 6,711 words (English) and 13,386 characters (Chinese).
extraction.creator: Yushi Bai, Xin Lv, Jiajie Zhang, Hongchang Lyu, Jiankai Tang, Zhidian Huang, Zhengxiao Du, Xiao Liu, Aohan Zeng, Lei Hou, Yuxiao Dong, Jie Tang, Juanzi Li
extraction.rai:dataCollection: LongBench comprises datasets collected from multiple sources including existing datasets (NarrativeQA, Qasper, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue, DuReader, GovReport, QMSum, MultiNews) and manually curated datasets (MultiFieldQA-en and MultiFieldQA-zh). For manually curated datasets, documents were collected from legal documents, government reports, encyclopedias, and academic papers, with three Ph.D. students annotating questions and answers. For multi-document QA tasks, complete Wikipedia passages were used, with supporting and distracting passages randomly ordered. The DuReader dataset was adapted by providing 20 documents per question including distractors.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include: literature and film documents (NarrativeQA), NLP papers (Qasper), legal documents, government reports, encyclopedias, academic papers (MultiFieldQA), Wikipedia passages (HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue), Baidu Search and Baidu Zhidao documents (DuReader), government reports (GovReport), meeting transcripts (QMSum), and news articles (MultiNews).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For MultiFieldQA datasets, three Ph.D. students annotated questions and answers for each article with definitive answers. Annotators ensured answers could be inferred from documents and evidence placement was fairly random to avoid biases. For other datasets, questions were written by native speakers (HotpotQA), synthesized through manually designed templates (2WikiMultihopQA), composed from simple questions and paraphrased by annotators (MuSiQue), or extracted from existing datasets.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Three Ph.D. students for MultiFieldQA datasets; native speakers for HotpotQA; NLP practitioners for Qasper
extraction.rai:dataBiases: During annotation, placement of evidence was randomized to avoid biases that might occur if answer-related statements are frequently found at the beginning or the end of documents.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark focuses on texts up to tens of thousands of tokens in length. Questions in MultiFieldQA are designed with definitive answers for ease of automated evaluation, which may limit the complexity of questions that can be asked.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The benchmark is designed for evaluating long context understanding capabilities of large language models across multiple tasks including single-doc QA, multi-doc QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code completion. All datasets are standardized into a unified format allowing for effortless automatic evaluation of LLMs.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For multi-document QA, supporting passages are included within the context, then distracting passages are added until the total length reaches a maximum length, and these passages are randomly ordered. For DuReader, several documents related to the question are provided along with arbitrarily selected distractors until each question is associated with 20 documents. Two extraction strategies are employed: random sampling to maintain natural length distribution, and uniform sampling based on data length to study model capabilities across varying context lengths.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data is extracted from test sets of public datasets to avoid test leakage. All datasets in LongBench are standardized into a unified format for automatic evaluation. For multi-document QA, complete Wikipedia passages are utilized encompassing supporting or distracting paragraphs. During annotation for MultiFieldQA, answers are ensured to be inferable from documents with evidence placement fairly randomized to avoid biases.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: To tailor the data for long-context evaluation, we utilize complete Wikipedia passages encompassing the supporting or distracting paragraphs as the context. Initially, supporting passages are included within the context, and then as many distracting passages are added until the total length reaches a maximum length. Finally, these passages are randomly ordered to form the multi-document context... for each question, we not only provide several documents related to the question but also arbitrarily select several from the total set of documents as distractors, until each question is associated with 20 documents... We employ two extraction strategies: random sampling and uniform sampling.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Since LLMs may have already been trained on the training set of some of our collected public datasets, to avoid test leakage, we extract data from the test sets of these public datasets...
